inputs.share_count_basis: 147.25m shares outstanding net of treasury at 30 June 2026 (Q1 FY2027 tanshin), LESS ~6.3m shares for the unexecuted balance (~JPY12.6bn of the JPY15bn / up-to-13m-share programme running June 2026 to March 2027, at ~JPY2,000) = ~141.0m pro forma. The cash for that balance is deducted in equity_bridge so the shrinking count is charged once, not credited for free. Held FLAT thereafter: future buybacks are funded from the FCF already in the equity value and are value-neutral at IV. No dilutive instruments of note (restricted-stock remuneration JPY159m/yr).
inputs.sbc_source: SBC-zero market convention: the only share-based pay is transfer-restricted stock remuneration of JPY159m in FY2026 (annual tanshin, statement of changes in equity; 0.07% of revenue), treated as zero so the house/street band collapses (band_position null). No stock options; equity-award taxes nil.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2026 purchase of treasury stock JPY16,581m (annual tanshin line 959); FY2025 JPY7,882m. New JPY15bn programme launched June 2026 runs to March 2027 (Evolution2035 cash plan: JPY44bn shareholder returns over FY2027-29 incl. dividends at 40%+ payout).
inputs.wacc_rationale: JPY-built. 10y JGB ~1.7%, Japan ERP ~5.5-6%, beta ~0.9-1.0 for a diversified chemicals/auto-safety/pharma group gives a cost of equity ~7-7.5%; ~15% debt weight at ~1% after-tax cost pulls a market WACC toward 6.5%. House reference for JPY keiretsu industrials is ~9%; Nippon Kayaku is less cyclical than a pure auto supplier (30% of revenue is pharma/agrochemicals), so 8.0% is used. Same WACC in all three scenarios: cyclicality and execution risk are charged in the driver paths and the weights, not in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: J-GAAP filer; operating leases are expensed inside operating income and no IFRS-16 right-of-use liabilities exist, so no lease adjustment is made (treatment: already an operating cost). total_debt is loans + bonds only.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests JPY1,113m (30 June 2026) deducted once in equity_bridge; flows are consolidated. NCI profit share is ~JPY0.2bn/yr, immaterial.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (operating company route per dcf-methods SKILL.md; non-US/cyclical adaptations applied: JPY WACC, J-GAAP leases, NCI once, matching-asset rule for the cross-shareholding portfolio, SBC-near-zero so house/street band collapses). Base year: the margin path is anchored to FY2027 guidance (sales JPY270.9bn, OI JPY27.3bn, raised Aug 2026 after Q1 +23% sales / +54% OI), NOT to FY2024's depressed OI (JPY7.3bn: JPY6.0bn AnHeart licensing upfront in SG&A + semiconductor inventory downturn + raw-material inflation) and NOT to FY2026's reported FCF of JPY3.9bn, which was depressed by an investment-cycle capex of JPY24.9bn (FY2025: JPY30.4bn) against D&A of JPY15.6bn. Mid-cycle: the base mature EBITDA margin of 17.5% equals the FY2017-FY2026 average excluding the FY2024 outlier (17.7%); capex normalises from the Evolution2035 Phase-1 level (~JPY30bn/yr = 11-12% of sales, plus in-licensing: long-term prepaid expenses rose JPY15.6bn in Q1 FY2027) to the 10-year average of ~8% of sales. Flows are built from operating income, so interest income (JPY571m) and dividend income (JPY927m) on the JPY34.1bn investment-securities portfolio are excluded from the flows and the portfolio is added in the bridge at fair value less a 25% haircut (tax on embedded gains; the company is selling ~JPY18bn of cross-shareholdings over FY2027-29). FY label convention: repo FY2027 = year ending 31 March 2027 = the company's own 'FY2026'; Evolution2035 Phase-1 targets (JPY300bn sales, JPY36bn OI, ROE 10%+, ROIC 7%+ by company FY2028) therefore fall in repo FY2029. From Q1 FY2027 domestic PP&E depreciation moved from declining-balance to straight-line (+JPY189m/quarter to OI) -- cash-neutral, modelled as a slightly lower D&A % that rebuilds as the Phase-1 capex enters service. Price is the 30 Oct 2026 regular close, not after-hours.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: blend: FY2027 guidance (+12%) and Evolution2035 Phase-1 (JPY300bn by repo FY2029, ~5%/yr thereafter) decaying to 1.5%; equity CAGR (4.2%) is depressed by JPY24bn of buybacks over two years and EPS CAGR is inflated by FY2026 securities gains, so neither is a clean anchor
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS 5yr CAGR 17.0% vs equity 5yr CAGR 4.2% and revenue 6.9%: divergence >30%. EPS is flattered by the FY2021 trough base, FY2026 investment-securities gains (JPY9.4bn) and a 14% lower share count. Owner-FCF CAGRs are negative because FY2025-26 carried an investment-cycle capex of JPY55bn against JPY30bn of D&A; they measure the capex cycle, not earning power.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - interest income, JPY m): FY2021 11,052; FY2022 13,855; FY2023 6,952; FY2024 6,935; FY2025 -5,775; FY2026 3,349 (3,190 after the JPY159m restricted-stock charge). EBITDA margin FY2017-26: 19.5, 20.4, 18.5, 17.1, 16.2, 18.7, 17.7, 10.5, 15.4, 15.7 (avg ex-FY2024 17.7%). Capex/sales 10-yr avg 8.5%.

base.narrative: FY2027 lands on the raised guidance (sales +12%, OI JPY27.3bn = 10.1% margin; EBITDA 15.9% with straight-line D&A ~6.0% of sales). Sales reach the JPY300bn Phase-1 target in repo FY2029 (+5.5%, +5.0%) but OI gets only ~75% of the targeted step-up (16.9% EBITDA / ~10.7% OI margin vs the 12% target) because Mobility & Imaging pass-through of raw-material costs lags, as it did in FY2026. Mature EBITDA margin 17.5% = the FY2017-26 average ex-FY2024. Capex runs at the Phase-1 plan (~JPY30bn/yr plus in-licensing) for three years then normalises to 7.5% of sales. Growth decays to 1.5% (Japan nominal GDP). Cash tax 30% (statutory ~30.5%). WC absorbs 20% of each year's revenue increase.

bull.narrative: Evolution2035 Phase 1 delivered in full and early: AI-server/advanced-packaging demand keeps Fine Chemicals compounding at high single digits, inflator share gains in China/Global South and pricing revisions restore Mobility & Imaging margins, IBTROZI and biosimilars lift Life Science. Sales pass JPY300bn in repo FY2029 (+13%, +8%, +7%) and OI margin reaches 12%+ (EBITDA 18-19%), i.e. the JPY36bn OI target is met; mature EBITDA margin 19.0% approaches the FY2017-18 peak (19.5-20.4%). Terminal growth 1.5%.

bear.narrative: FY2027 misses guidance (+8% sales, EBITDA 15.0%) as US auto tariffs and a global auto production slowdown hit Mobility & Imaging while raw-material inflation again outruns pass-through; the AI-materials cycle turns in FY2028-29 (a repeat of the FY2024 Fine Chemicals inventory correction) and Japan drug-price revisions cut Life Science; Evolution2035 is pushed out and inorganic spend (licences, M&A) consumes cash without returns. EBITDA margin troughs at 13.5% and recovers only to 15.0%, roughly the FY2025-26 level; growth 1-2%. Capex is cut to 7% of sales. Terminal growth 0.5%.

scenario_narratives.base: Guidance-year FY2027 as raised (sales JPY270.9bn, OI JPY27.3bn); sales reach the JPY300bn Evolution2035 Phase-1 target by repo FY2029 but OI margin gets ~75% of the way to the 12% target; mature EBITDA margin 17.5% (10-year average ex-FY2024); capex at the Phase-1 plan (~JPY30bn/yr incl. licensing) then normalising to 7.5% of sales; growth decaying to 1.5%; WACC 8.0% JPY; terminal growth 1.0%, cap 15x.
scenario_narratives.bull: Phase 1 met in full (JPY300bn / JPY36bn OI by repo FY2029) on the AI-materials cycle, inflator share gains and pricing recovery in Mobility & Imaging plus new oncology/biosimilar launches; mature EBITDA margin 19.0%; terminal growth 1.5%.
scenario_narratives.bear: Auto downturn plus tariffs and a semiconductor inventory correction in FY2028-29 with raw-material inflation unrecovered; EBITDA margin troughs 13.5% and plateaus at 15.0%; growth 1-2%; Evolution2035 inorganic spend earns nothing; terminal growth 0.5%.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 20%: ~70% of revenue (Mobility & Imaging + Fine Chemicals) is tied to global auto production and the semiconductor cycle, and FY2024/FY2026 both showed how fast segment profit can drop (OI -66% in FY2024; M&I segment profit -20% in FY2026 on raw materials). Bull cut from 35% to 30%: the bull case needs the AI-materials cycle, inflator pricing recovery and Life Science launches all to land, and the prior KV25 plan missed its profit targets. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Nippon Kayaku as a mid-cycle diversified chemicals group: anchor the near term to the raised FY2027 guidance, give partial credit to the Evolution2035 margin targets, and capitalise a mature 17.5% EBITDA margin that is the company's own ten-year average rather than either the FY2024 trough or the FY2017-18 peak. Charge the full Phase-1 investment programme (capex plus in-licensing) before letting capex normalise, charge the cross-shareholdings' income out of the flows and add the portfolio back in the bridge, and shrink the share count only for the buyback whose cash is also deducted. Discount in JPY at 8.0% with no per-scenario WACC premium; cyclicality lives in the bear path and its 20% weight.
key_risks_to_valuation: Raw-material (naphtha-derivative) cost inflation outrunning price pass-through in Mobility & Imaging, as in FY2026 (segment profit -20%)
Global auto production and US tariff policy -- the largest segment sells into OEMs/Tier-1s; a production slowdown or tariff escalation hits volumes directly
Semiconductor/AI-materials cycle turning (Fine Chemicals fell to JPY5.2bn segment profit in FY2024 from JPY10.6bn)
Japan NHI drug-price revisions compressing Life Science margins faster than IBTROZI/biosimilar launches offset

Evolution2035 inorganic spend (licences such as the JPY15.6bn long-term prepaid booked in Q1 FY2027, M&A) consuming cash without returns -- the model charges Phase-1 capex but cannot see the returns on licences
Terminal value is ~60% of EV; each 1pp of WACC is worth ~JPY250-300/share
Investment-securities bridge (JPY25.6bn after haircut, ~JPY180/share) depends on disposal proceeds and tax; the company plans only ~JPY18bn of sales over three years
